beforeImage.name: Valentra
beforeImage.description: Valentra is a carved-out platform of chemical pipeline infrastructure on the U.S. Gulf Coast. The business serves industrial chemical producers and storage users through pipeline-connected sites and related infrastructure used for the handling of methanol-based intermediates and related products. Its operating model is asset-heavy and infrastructure-like, with revenues tied to essential transport and storage capabilities rather than commodity production. Ancala acquired the portfolio from Hexion in December 2025 and established Valentra as the operating platform. Reviewed public sources do not disclose Ancala's ownership percentage or the detailed financing structure.

afterImage.name: Valentra
afterImage.subsector: Formalin production and chemical pipeline infrastructure
afterImage.description: Valentra is a U.S. Gulf Coast producer of formalin products and operator of associated chemical infrastructure. Its pipeline-connected sites in Baytown, Texas; Luling, Louisiana; and Geismar, Louisiana combine production, storage, pipelines, rail access and barge docks to supply co-located chemical plants and offsite industrial customers under large-volume, multi-year contracts. Its products support agriculture, healthcare, automotive, construction, resins, paints and coatings, consumer goods and other industrial end markets. Ancala Partners acquired the business from Hexion and formed Valentra as a standalone platform on December 4, 2025. Financial terms, Ancala's exact stake and its fund vehicle were not publicly disclosed.

milestones.event: Alex Mihut joined Valentra as CEO to lead its transition into a standalone platform and its future growth.
Financing for the acquisition was arranged and disclosed by transaction advisers.
